Q137911647.summary: Under a round-headed arch, the dead Christ is lowered from the cross: one figure supports his body while another, kneeling, draws the nail from his feet, and mourners stand at either side, with further figures above the cross. The small carving gathers the grief and tenderness of the moment into a tight, devotional composition.
facts: Wikidata records the relief as pearwood, about 26.7 cm high, in the Bode-Museum's Romanesque sculpture collection.
Q137911647.notes: Only Wikidata and Commons were available (the museum's online database was down). The Commons file name links the relief to Trier, which could not be confirmed. The identity of the mourners is not certain from the photograph.

cur:catacombs-three-shepherds-sarcophagu.summary: Three shepherds carrying sheep stand on pedestals at the ends and centre, while the whole surface between them is filled with vines in which winged putti harvest and tread the grapes. The vintage, a symbol of the Eucharist and of paradise, surrounds the Good Shepherd, the image of Christ caring for the souls of the dead.
facts: The sarcophagus is displayed in the Museo Pio Cristiano and dated by Commons to the second half of the 4th century.
The motif of the grape harvest by putti was shared with pagan Dionysiac art and given new meaning in Christian use.
cur:catacombs-three-shepherds-sarcophagu.notes: The Good Shepherd figures are symbolic; their identification with Christ is an interpretation, well established in this Christian context.
